title: The first stones of the breastplate and their powers
english: From the holy Epiphanius, on the twelve stones fixed in the breastplate of the priest.

Sardion, the stone called Babylonian, is fiery-red and blood-like in appearance. It is found in Babylon, in the land toward Assyria. It is translucent and has healing power, and doctors use it by anointing with it for swellings and wounds caused by iron.

Topazion is red, more so than the anthrax stone. It is found in Topaze, a city of India. When it is rubbed on a medical whetstone, it does not yield a red juice matching its color, but a milky one. It fills mixing bowls—many of them, as many as the person rubbing it wishes—and it is not diminished either in weight or in circumference. The juice rubbed from it is useful for afflictions of the eyes, and when drunk it helps with water-madness and with those driven mad by sea-grape.
Smaragdos is green. The barbarians dig it up in the Indian mountains and cut it. Its power is for the mirroring of faces.

Anthrax is bright-red in appearance. It is found in Carthage in Libya, which is called Africa. They say it is found not by day but by night, for from far off it sparkles like a torch or a coal, and ceases for an hour. Those who seek it recognize that this is the stone, go toward its gleam, and find it. And when it is carried, whatever clothes it is wrapped in, its gleam shines outside the camp.
